Hace más de 20.000 años, cazadores pinta: More than 20,000 years ago, hunters painted the walls of Cueva de la Pileta, about 11 km to the southwest. Later, Neolithic and Bronze Age groups farmed and kept livestock in the Serranía. The plateau above El Tajo was still empty.
Un pequeño poblado fortificado crece en: A small fortified settlement grew on the plateau south of El Tajo. Cliffs protected it on three sides. The name Arunda probably comes from this period.
Tras la Segunda Guerra Púnica, Roma cont: After the Second Punic War, Rome controlled the region. Arunda was a small town. The main Roman town was Acinipo, about 11 km to the northwest, with a theatre from the 1st century BC.
El mundo romano se rompe. Los reyes visi: The Roman world broke apart. Visigothic kings ruled from Toledo. Very few remains from this period survive in Ronda.
Tropas bereberes llegan después del año: Berber troops arrived after 711. The town, now Izna Rand Onda, belonged to the district of Takurunna. Walls, a citadel and the medina took shape on the plateau. The revolt of Umar ibn Hafsún (880–928) shook the surrounding mountains.
Cuando cae el Califato de Córdoba, los B: After the fall of the Caliphate of Córdoba, the Banu Ifran ruled a small independent kingdom from Ronda. The taifa of Seville conquered it in 1065.
Ronda es una fortaleza en la frontera co: Ronda was a fortress on the frontier with Castile. The Arab baths, the water mine at Casa del Rey Moro and the Almocábar gate date from this period. Suburbs grew outside the walls beside the river.
Fernando el Católico toma Ronda tras un: Ferdinand the Catholic took Ronda after a short siege. The main mosque became the church of Santa María la Mayor. A market district, El Mercadillo, grew north of El Tajo. Puente Viejo was rebuilt in 1616.
Un primer puente sobre el Tajo se hunde: The first bridge over El Tajo collapsed in 1741. Puente Nuevo was built between 1759 and 1793, to a design by José Martín de Aldehuela. The Real Maestranza bullring opened in 1785.
Las tropas francesas ocupan Ronda durant: French troops occupied Ronda during the Peninsular War and blew up the citadel when they left in 1812. Bandits from the Serranía and Romantic travellers made Ronda famous. The railway from Bobadilla to Algeciras arrived in 1892.
El poeta Rainer Maria Rilke vive en Rond: The poet Rainer Maria Rilke lived in Ronda in 1912–13. In 1918, the Assembly of Ronda adopted the flag and coat of arms of Andalusia. The town grew towards the railway station.
La Guerra Civil trae la violencia a Rond: The Civil War brought violence to Ronda in 1936. New housing blocks appeared north of El Mercadillo in the 1950s and 1960s. Aerial photographs from 1956 provide the first complete image of the town.
Nuevos barrios y un polígono industrial: New neighbourhoods and an industrial estate grew north of the railway. Tourism became the main industry in the town.
Los años 2000 son la década con más edif: The 2000s have the most new buildings in the land registry. Dates for buildings after 1956 come directly from the land registry.

Litografía basada en un dibujo de Teniso: Lithograph based on a drawing by Tenison.
La Pileta conserva animales y signos pin: La Pileta preserves animals and signs painted in prehistory. Neolithic finds also come from Ronda’s old town: the plateau was not always empty. The layout of those early settlements is unknown.
En La Pileta conviven pinturas paleolíti: Palaeolithic paintings and later schematic designs coexist at La Pileta. They do not belong to a single date: the cave holds traces of several periods.
Abre el plano de La Pileta y compara sus: Open the plan of La Pileta and compare its passages with the cave photograph.
El paisaje sin edificios es una simplifi: The landscape without buildings is a visual simplification, not evidence that nobody lived here. The start of the scale is approximate.
Antes del dominio romano, Ronda y Acinip: Before Roman rule, Ronda and Acinipo already had a long history of settlement. Their plateaus overlooked the surrounding land and nearby farmland. Archaeology cannot show every house or establish a single foundation date.
Acinipo conserva restos anteriores a Rom: Acinipo preserves remains from before Rome, although the theatre that dominates the site today is Roman. A ruin in a photograph did not necessarily exist throughout the site’s history.
Busca el borde de la meseta: el relieve: Look for the edge of the plateau: the terrain helps explain where people settled.
Las casas de esta etapa son ilustrativas: The houses in this period are illustrative. No single Celtic identity or exact foundation date is assigned without evidence.
Arunda, bajo la actual Ronda, y Acinipo: Arunda, beneath modern Ronda, and Acinipo were distinct settlements. Acinipo preserves a theatre, baths and Roman houses. Its nickname “Ronda la Vieja” can mislead: it does not mean the whole town moved from one site to the other.
En el teatro de Acinipo, el graderío apr: At Acinipo’s theatre, the seating follows the slope of the rock. The terrain forms part of the building itself.
Abre la foto del teatro y observa los as: Open the theatre photo and look at the seating cut into the slope. Acinipo lies outside this 3D map.
206 a. C. sirve de referencia regional p: 206 BC is a regional reference for Rome’s advance, not a proven foundation date for Arunda.
Una ciudad difícil de reconstruir: A town that is hard to reconstruct
Acinipo pierde importancia durante los ú: Acinipo lost importance in the later Roman centuries, while Arunda became more prominent. Surviving remains are fragmentary. Small objects offer evidence where a detailed plan of the town is missing.
El ladrillo funerario de la galería proc: The funerary brick in the gallery comes from Acinipo and is catalogued to the 4th–6th centuries. It is an ancient object photographed in a museum, not an image of a street from that time.
Abre el ladrillo y observa sus letras y: Open the brick photograph and look at its lettering and moulded designs.
Los límites 411–711 organizan el relato;: The dates 411–711 organise the story; houses did not change instantly at those boundaries. The later rock-cut church of La Cabeza appears in the next period.
Ronda y la cora de Takurunna: Ronda and the district of Takurunna
Durante el periodo islámico, Ronda se co: During the Islamic period, Ronda developed as a town and capital of Takurunna, a district of al-Andalus. Urban life centred on the plateau now called La Ciudad. The surviving defences changed over several centuries.
Frente a Ronda, la iglesia rupestre de l: Opposite Ronda, the rock-cut church of Virgen de la Cabeza dates from the 9th–10th centuries. It is evidence of Christian communities during the Andalusi period.
Compara las habitaciones excavadas de La: Compare the rooms cut into the rock at La Cabeza with buildings on the plateau.
711 marca el comienzo de la conquista de: 711 marks the start of the conquest of the peninsula, not a verified date for each building in Ronda.
Al fragmentarse el poder de Córdoba, Ron: As Córdoba’s power fragmented, Ronda became a taifa: an independent kingdom. Its autonomy ended when Seville absorbed it in 1065. For several decades, the town was a political capital, although its exact extent remains uncertain.
«Taifa» designa uno de los reinos surgid: A taifa was one of the kingdoms formed as al-Andalus fragmented. A change of ruler did not mean a new neighbourhood appeared at once.
Mira la posición de La Ciudad sobre el T: Look at La Ciudad above El Tajo: its position helps explain its defensive value.
El comienzo de esta taifa tiene datacion: Sources give different dates for the start of this taifa. Around 1039 is a conventional point in the tour, not an undisputed foundation date. The photograph shows surviving defences altered later.
En los siglos XIII–XV, Ronda ocupa una p: In the 13th–15th centuries, Ronda held a strategic position between Granada, Castile and North Africa. Below the medina, San Miguel contained houses and workshops. Its Arab baths were built beside the water in the 13th–14th centuries.
El hammam tenía salas fría, templada y c: The hammam had cold, warm and hot rooms. A waterwheel supplied water and heat passed beneath the floor. It was a place for washing and social life, not a modern swimming pool.
Abre la foto interior de los baños y bus: Open the interior photograph of the baths and look for the star-shaped skylights.
El título resume un periodo largo: la co: The title covers a long period: the Nasrid frontier belongs mainly to its later centuries. The surviving minaret dates from the 14th century, with a later Christian upper section.
El 22 de mayo de 1485, las tropas de Fer: On 22 May 1485, Ferdinand the Catholic’s troops took Ronda. The conquest changed house ownership and the organisation of the town. The main mosque became Santa María la Mayor; new squares and convents altered the old medina.
El Puente Viejo conserva una fábrica de: Puente Viejo’s present structure dates from 1616. Before Puente Nuevo, reaching El Mercadillo from the lower gorge meant climbing steep streets.
Compara la altura del Puente Viejo con l: Compare the height of Puente Viejo with the plateau where El Mercadillo would grow.
Las fotos muestran edificios conservados: The photographs show buildings preserved and altered over centuries, not their exact appearance in 1485.
El primer puente sobre la parte alta del: The first bridge across the upper gorge collapsed in 1741. A new project followed in 1751; work on Puente Nuevo began in 1759 and ended in 1793. Meanwhile, the bullring officially opened on 19 May 1785.
La plaza comenzó a levantarse de forma d: Permanent construction of the bullring began in 1779. Its archive records performances before completion and difficulties during construction. The building took shape over time, rather than on a single day.
Sigue cómo el puente une las dos mesetas: Watch the bridge connect the two plateaus: it changes how people cross and move through the town.
1751 corresponde al proyecto y 1759 al i: The University of Seville distinguishes the 1751 project from construction starting in 1759. Aldehuela completed work involving several master builders.
La ciudad entra en las fotografías: The town enters the photographic record
Los grabados y las primeras fotografías: Prints and early photographs show a Ronda of mills, paths and travellers. The Alameda dates from 1806. Ronda station opened in September 1891: the railway changed connections for a town surrounded by mountains.
En la fotografía de Carl Curman de 1878: Carl Curman’s 1878 photograph shows Los Molinos below the bridge. Compare the valley buildings with the town above: this landscape was also a place of work.
Abre «Los Molinos, 1878» y busca los edi: Open “Los Molinos, 1878” and look for buildings now missing at the foot of El Tajo.
ADIF fecha la estación en 1891. No se co: ADIF dates the station to 1891. Its opening is not confused with completion of the whole line. Prints and photographs carry their own dates.
Los días 13 y 14 de enero de 1918, la As: On 13–14 January 1918, the Assembly of Ronda brought together the Andalusian regionalist movement. It adopted Andalusia’s green, white and green flag and its coat of arms. The meeting took place at Círculo de Artistas in Plaza del Socorro.
El escudo representa a Hércules entre do: The coat of arms shows Hercules between two columns, accompanied by two lions. A monument with these symbols stands in the square opposite the Assembly building.
Abre la fotografía del Círculo de Artist: Open the Círculo de Artistas photograph: it shows the Assembly building at a later date.
Las imágenes modernas del edificio y de: Modern photographs of the building and memorials are not photographs of the 1918 meeting.
La Guerra Civil rompe la vida de la ciud: The Civil War shattered life in the town. On 16 September 1936, Ronda fell to the rebel forces; families fled and Francoist repression followed. Decades later, aerial photographs allow detailed comparisons of streets, gardens and new neighbourhoods.
El vuelo americano Serie B se realizó en: The American Series B survey took place in 1956–57. It is a reference for this project, but not Spain’s first survey: IGN also preserves Series A from 1945–46. Ronda’s historic town received protection in 1966.
Compara la imagen aérea con la ciudad ac: Compare the aerial image with the town today: look for fields that later became streets.
No se utilizan escenas literarias de Hem: Literary scenes by Hemingway are not used as evidence of specific events. The history of victims requires documentary evidence.
Las elecciones municipales del 3 de abri: The local elections of 3 April 1979 began a new period of municipal government. Aerial surveys from the following decades show Ronda’s transformation: streets, housing and facilities extending beyond the historic centre.
El «Vuelo Interministerial» abarca campa: The “Interministerial survey” covers campaigns between 1973 and 1986. That range identifies an image collection; it does not mean every photograph was taken in 1980.
Mira el entorno de la estación y compara: Look around the station and compare the built-up areas with the 1956–57 survey.
Las fechas de las capas aéreas son rango: Aerial layers use survey ranges when the capture date has not been verified. The blend between images is a visual transition, not a film of the town growing.
Ronda es una ciudad habitada, además de: Ronda is a living town as well as a historic landscape. IECA records 33,708 residents in the municipality in 2025. El Tajo became a Natural Monument in 2019, recognising the Guadalevín gorge, the bridge and wildlife on its cliffs.
En las paredes del Tajo habitan aves com: Birds including the lesser kestrel and chough live on the cliffs of El Tajo. Landscape protection covers both natural and cultural value.
Prueba una vista desde el río y otra des: Try a river view and a town view: the same bridge reveals two different landscapes.
La fecha del deslizador no es la fecha d: The slider date is not the date of every image. Aerial detail for El Tajo, the station and the northeast is from July 2022. The 3D buildings and their dates remain approximate.

Plano publicado en 2010 de las galerías: A plan of La Pileta’s passages published in 2010. It is a modern guide, not a prehistoric drawing.

Acinipo en 2009. El lugar tuvo ocupación: Acinipo in 2009. The site was occupied before Rome, but the large visible wall belongs to the later Roman theatre.
Plano moderno del yacimiento de Acinipo,: A modern plan of Acinipo published in 2014. It includes Roman buildings from after this period; it does not represent a complete pre-Roman settlement.
Paisaje pintado por Frederic Leighton en: A landscape painted by Frederic Leighton between 1886 and 1889. It is a 19th-century artist’s view of the area around Ronda.
Teatro romano de Acinipo en 2009. El gra: Acinipo’s Roman theatre in 2009. Its seating follows the hillside and is cut into the rock. Acinipo is a separate site from Arunda beneath Ronda.
Ilustración de una moneda de Acinipo en: An illustration of an Acinipo coin in an 1854 dictionary of ancient geography. The depicted coin is ancient; the printed drawing is from the 19th century.
Pieza de arcilla moldeada procedente de: A moulded clay object from Acinipo, catalogued to the 4th–6th centuries. It belongs to Toledo’s Museo Sefardí; this photograph was taken at an exhibition in Paris in 2022.
Interior excavado en la roca de la Virge: The rock-cut interior of Virgen de la Cabeza, photographed in 2010. The complex dates from the 9th–10th centuries: the Andalusi period, not the Visigothic period.
Alminar de San Sebastián en 2018. Los do: San Sebastián minaret in 2018. The lower two sections date from the 14th century; the upper section was added in the Christian period. It is not an 8th-century building.
Defensas medievales conservadas, fotogra: Surviving medieval defences, photographed in 2010. The visible walls include alterations from different periods and cannot alone reconstruct the 8th-century town.
Puerta del alminar de San Sebastián, fot: Doorway of San Sebastián minaret, photographed in 2011. The surviving minaret is from the 14th century, later than the 11th-century taifa kingdom.
Ronda’s walls photographed in 2010. They help locate the medina on the plateau; their surviving and restored sections should not all be dated to the 11th century.
Interior de los baños árabes de Ronda en: Inside Ronda’s Arab baths in 2024. The vaults and skylights reveal the architecture of this 13th–14th-century complex.
Vista exterior del recinto de los baños: An exterior view of the baths in 2010. It shows the remains of their rooms; this photograph does not show the vaulted interior.
The façade of Casa del Rey Moro in 2003. The house dates from the 18th century; the medieval water mine below it is not visible in this photograph.
Litografía publicada en Castile and Anda: A lithograph published in Castile and Andalusia in 1853, based on a drawing by Tenison. It depicts the completed bridge, sixty years after its inauguration.
Grabado anónimo publicado en The Wayside: An anonymous print published in The Wayside Cross in 1847. It is an artistic view made after the bridge was built.
Carl Curman fotografió Los Molinos en 18: Carl Curman photographed Los Molinos in 1878. Puente Nuevo appears on the left; the valley buildings reveal a working landscape that has since changed.
Grabado de Gustave Doré publicado en L’E: A print by Gustave Doré published in Davillier’s L’Espagne in 1874. Its original title says “Pont Romain”; that historical name alone does not prove Roman origins.
Gaucín, en una publicación de 1838 asoci: Gaucín, in an 1838 publication associated with David Roberts. This is another town in the Serranía, not a view of Ronda itself.
Estación de Ronda fotografiada en julio: Ronda station photographed in July 2009. ADIF dates its opening to September 1891. This photograph shows the building long after it opened.
Vista desde el Puente Nuevo conservada p: A view from Puente Nuevo held by Hallwylska museet. The catalogue dates it to before 1895; it is not a photograph from 1900.
Monumento a Rainer Maria Rilke, realizad: A memorial to Rainer Maria Rilke, made by Nicomedes Díaz Piquero in 1966 and photographed in 2008. It is a later tribute to the poet, not a photograph of his stay in Ronda.
Círculo de Artistas en septiembre de 200: Círculo de Artistas in September 2008. This building in Plaza del Socorro hosted the Assembly of Ronda in January 1918.
Recorte de la ortofoto del vuelo america: A crop from IGN’s American Series B orthophoto. The survey dates from 1956–57; the exact capture date of this frame has not been verified here.
Homenaje a Ernest Hemingway fotografiado: A tribute to Ernest Hemingway photographed in 2016. It is a modern memorial, not a Civil War photograph or evidence of an event described in a novel.
Trajes expuestos en el museo de la plaza: Costumes displayed in the bullring museum, photographed in 2013. These are exhibition objects, not a photograph of a bullfight during the dictatorship.
Recorte de la colección Interministerial: A crop from IGN’s Interministerial collection, covering surveys from 1973–1986. That range is retained: the file name does not establish a capture date of 1980.
El Guadalevín bajo el Puente Viejo, foto: The Guadalevín below Puente Viejo, photographed by Diego Delso in March 2005.
